newsitem.title: UK: NATWEST TO ANNOUNCE LOSS FINDINGS THIS WEEK.
newsitem.headline: NATWEST TO ANNOUNCE LOSS FINDINGS THIS WEEK.

text.p: NatWest Markets, the investment banking arm of Britain's National Westminster Bank Plc, said on Monday it could announce early findings about its 50 million pound ($80 million) options loss later this week.
But a full report is some way off. "There may be an announcement about preliminary findings later this week but the full report will not be completed for some weeks," a spokeswoman told Reuters.
British newspapers have said NatWest is expected to deal severely with any managers found by the inquiry to have been lacking. But the bank declined to comment on what measures may be taken.
"We are trying to be fair but also want to find the lines of accountability that matter," the firm's spokeswoman said, adding it was trying to be as quick as possible but also thorough and accurate.
It has appointed independent firms to check its investigation. Accountants Coopers & Lybrand and lawyers Linklaters and Paines were brought in after the bank made the embarrassing revelation.
The 50 million pound hole in its interest rate options book, which it put down to "mispricing errors", was announced at the end of last month, only days after its 1996 results were released.

NatWest has reported a former trader, said by banking sources to be Kyriacos Papouis, to financial watchdog the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) and suspended a senior trader, named by banking sources as Neil Dodgson, for "failure to supervise".
Last Friday Papouis, who last December left NatWest for U.S. investment bank Bear Stearns, had resigned from his new employer, where he was an interest rate trader.

Bear Stearns declined to give any details of his resignation, except to say it had conducted a thorough review of his open trading positions and was satisfied they were all booked and managed properly.
Options are contracts which give buyers the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an underlying security at a set price on a set date in the future.
The SFA has been notified of the NatWest internal probe into the loss and has opened a file while the Bank of England has said it is co-operating with the SFA. ($ = 0.625 British Pounds)
